<reason>B won by turning a real problem into a comparative instrument test and making that test easier to decide: credits help late, least those with the thinnest records, and can substitute for help that actually reaches caregivers now. A stayed closer to the motion and landed a clean bind on writing “zero,” but never squarely neutralized regressivity, timing, or crowd-out. B answered A’s pressure honestly, then weighed those remaining holes more cleanly than A answered B’s.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s second rebuttal: keeping the contribution record at zero as financing, not worth; contrasting need-targeted transfers with deferred “earned” credits; then stacking unanswered regressivity, timeline, and crowd-out.</best_rebuttal>
